newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt tourism chamber says may set up own airline.
newsitem.headline: Egypt tourism chamber says may set up own airline.

text.p: The Egyptian Chamber of Tourism (ECT) is considering setting up a private-sector domestic and international airline with a capital of no less than $30 million, a senior official said on Sunday.
Hamdi Saleh, head of the ECT, told Reuters that tourism companies would hold a preliminary meeting on March 17 to discuss the feasibility of such a project.

"We have not decided anything yet but we're thinking that the capital of the company should be no less than 100 million pounds and that it should operate on the local and international scene," Saleh said.
He said the ECT was thinking of buying airplanes from Ibrahim Kamel of the Kato group of companies, which signed a deal last year to buy 200 Russian Tupolev-204 jets powered by Rolls-Royce engines.
"This is one option and the prices are attractive for the quality we could be getting," Saleh said. "But then we could decide to rent planes or buy other planes."
Egypt's sole privately owned airline ZAS closed down in 1995 and industry sources said that it was forced out of business by state carrier EgyptAir.

EgyptAir chairman Mohamed Fahim Rayan said in remarks published in the government newspaper al-Akhbar that his company was not concerned by the competition a private ECT airline would generate but called on the chamber to limit its activity to charter flights that ferry tourists to Egypt.
"A company born of a 100 million pound capital is born small and this money will not enable it to buy planes or operate them, while we at EgyptAir have a fleet worth 9.1 billion pounds," Rayan said.

"But I hope this company will stick to charter flights... We in Egypt must work together, like other companies in the world, and we must maintain EgyptAir's performance and help it inside Egypt so that is remains to fly the flag throughout the world."
